name: Bread Cake
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: When you are making wheat bread, and the dough is quite light and ready to bake, take out as much of it as would make a twelve cent loaf
Mix with it a tea-cup full of powdered sugar, and a tea-cup full of butter that has been softened and stirred about in a tea-cup of warm milk
Knead it very well, put it into a square pan, dredged with flour
Cover it, and set it near the fire for half an hour
Bake it in a moderate oven, and wrap it in a thick cloth as soon as it is done

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. When you are making wheat bread, and the dough is quite light and ready to bake, take out as much of it as would make a twelve cent loaf
2. Mix with it a tea-cup full of powdered sugar, and a tea-cup full of butter that has been softened and stirred about in a tea-cup of warm milk
3. Add also a beaten egg
4. Knead it very well, put it into a square pan, dredged with flour
5. Cover it, and set it near the fire for half an hour
6. Bake it in a moderate oven, and wrap it in a thick cloth as soon as it is done
